# `silk/npm/config`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Read npm's configuration the way npm does: the built-in, global, user, and project `.npmrc`
files, `npm_config_*` environment variables, and command-line values, with `${VAR}` expansion,
scoped registries, and registry credentials.

## When to use
Use [`NpmConfig.load`](#NpmConfig.impl.load) in a tool that talks to an npm registry and must honor the user's
`.npmrc` files, such as a package manager or a publish script. Read a key with
[`NpmConfig.text`](#NpmConfig.impl.text), choose a registry for a package with [`NpmConfig.registryFor`](#NpmConfig.impl.registryFor), and get the
credentials for a request URL with [`NpmConfig.credentialsFor`](#NpmConfig.impl.credentialsFor). To parse one ini text without
layers, use `silk.npm.ini`.

## Details
A configuration is a list of layers. When two layers set a key, the one with the higher priority
wins. From highest to lowest, the layers are:

1. [`NpmConfigSource.CommandLine`](#NpmConfigSource.CommandLine): values the caller passes, such as parsed `--key=value`
   options.
2. [`NpmConfigSource.Environment`](#NpmConfigSource.Environment): each variable `npm_config_<name>` (any case) with a
   non-empty value. In `<name>`, each `_` after the first character becomes `-` and letters
   become lowercase, unless the name starts with `//`.
3. [`NpmConfigSource.Project`](#NpmConfigSource.Project): `.npmrc` in the project directory. That is the `prefix` from the
   command line, or else the nearest directory, from the working directory up, that has a
   `package.json` file or a `node_modules` directory. If a directory above it has a
   `package.json` whose `workspaces` patterns include it, that workspace root is used instead.
   The project file is skipped in global mode (`global` is `true` or `location` is `global`) and
   when it is the same file as the user file.
4. [`NpmConfigSource.User`](#NpmConfigSource.User): the `userconfig` file, by default `~/.npmrc`.
5. [`NpmConfigSource.Global`](#NpmConfigSource.Global): the `globalconfig` file, by default `<prefix>/etc/npmrc`.
6. [`NpmConfigSource.Builtin`](#NpmConfigSource.Builtin): the `npmrc` file in npm's own install directory, if the caller
   names it.

In every layer, `${NAME}` in a key or a text value is replaced by the environment variable
`NAME`. An unset variable leaves `${NAME}` as it is. A `\` before `$` stops the expansion, and
each pair of `\` before it becomes one `\`. As in npm, the items of a `key[]` list are expanded
only for npm's own list options: `ca`, `cidr`, `diff`, `include`, `noproxy`, `omit`, `package`,
and `workspace`. A file that cannot be read is an empty layer, as in npm. Keys inside an ini
`[section]` are ignored, as npm does not read them.

## Errors
- `HostInputError` if the environment or the working directory cannot be read.
- `FileError` if the working directory is not a valid absolute path.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the configuration.

## Gotchas
Values are not checked or converted with npm's table of option types: a value is text, a
boolean, a null, or a list, as the ini text gives it. npm's default values are not included,
except the default registry `https://registry.npmjs.org/`. npm finds its global prefix from the
path of the `node` program; here it comes from [`NpmConfigOptions`](#NpmConfigOptions), the `PREFIX` environment
variable, or a `prefix` key. Paths use the `/` form of `silk.system.filesystem`; on Windows pass
the paths in [`NpmConfigOptions`](#NpmConfigOptions).

## Examples
### Find the registry and the token for a scoped package
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.collections.bytes { Bytes }
import silk.collections.list { List }
import silk.system.host_input { HostInput, HostInputError }
import silk.npm.config { NpmConfig, NpmConfigSource, NpmCredentials }
import silk.system.filesystem { Path }

struct NoEnvironment {}

effect fn argumentCount(self: &mut NoEnvironment) -> usize ! HostInputError { return 0 }

effect fn argument(self: &mut NoEnvironment, index: usize) -> Option<Bytes>
  ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  return Option<Bytes>.none()
}

effect fn variable(self: &mut NoEnvironment, name: &[u8]) -> Option<Bytes>
  ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  return Option<Bytes>.none()
}

effect fn variableNames(self: &mut NoEnvironment) -> List<Bytes>
  ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  return List<Bytes>.make()
}

effect fn workingDirectory(self: &mut NoEnvironment) -> Bytes
  ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator {
  return run Bytes.copy(b"/")
}

impl HostInput for NoEnvironment {
  argumentCount: NoEnvironment.argumentCount
  argument: NoEnvironment.argument
  variable: NoEnvironment.variable
  variableNames: NoEnvironment.variableNames
  workingDirectory: NoEnvironment.workingDirectory
}

effect fn check() -> bool ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator {
  let mut config = NpmConfig.make()
  let text = b"@acme:registry=https://npm.acme.test/\n//npm.acme.test/:_authToken=secret\n"
  let layer = run NpmConfig.parseLayer(NpmConfigSource.User, Option<Path>.none(), text)
  run NpmConfig.addLayer(&mut config, move layer)
  let registry = NpmConfig.registryFor(&config, "@acme/widgets")
  let credentials = run NpmConfig.credentialsFor(&config, "https://npm.acme.test/@acme%2fwidgets", registry)
  return match move credentials {
    Option<NpmCredentials>.Some { value } => registry == "https://npm.acme.test/"
      && &NpmCredentials.token(&value) == &Option<string>.some("secret")
    Option<NpmCredentials>.None => false
  }
}

pub effect fn main() -> i32 ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  let mut environment = NoEnvironment {}
  let found = run check() |> Effect.provideMut<HostInput>(&mut environment)
    |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
  if !found {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="NpmCredentials"></a>

## `NpmCredentials`

```silk
pub struct NpmCredentials
```

The credentials that npm sends to a registry.

### Details

npm sends `Authorization: Bearer <token>` if there is a token, or else `Authorization: Basic
<basic>` if there is a basic value. [`NpmCredentials.authorization`](#NpmCredentials.impl.authorization) gives that header value.
A client certificate can come with either one, or alone.

The key prefix that had the credentials, such as `//registry.npmjs.org/`.

### Field `bearer`

```silk

```

The value of `<registryKey>:_authToken`.

```silk

```

The Base64 text for basic authentication: `<registryKey>:_auth` as written, or else

encoded.

<a id="NpmConfig"></a>

## `NpmConfig`

```silk
pub struct NpmConfig
```

npm's configuration: layers of keys, from the command line down to npm's built-in file.

### When to use

Use [`NpmConfig.load`](#NpmConfig.impl.load) to read the configuration that npm would use in a directory. Use
[`NpmConfig.make`](#NpmConfig.impl.make), [`NpmConfig.parseLayer`](#NpmConfig.impl.parseLayer), and [`NpmConfig.addLayer`](#NpmConfig.impl.addLayer) to build one from your
own text, for example in a test.

### Details

When two layers set a key, the higher one wins. From highest to lowest: command line,
environment, project, user, global, built-in.

<a id="NpmConfig.impl"></a>

```silk
impl NpmConfig
```

<a id="NpmConfig.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub fn make() -> NpmConfig
```

Returns a configuration with no layers, no home directory, and no working directory.

<a id="NpmConfig.impl.load"></a>

### Associated function `load`

```silk
pub effect fn load(options: NpmConfigOptions) -> NpmConfig
    ! HostInputError | FileError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut FileSystem | &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator
```

Reads npm's configuration for the working directory, from all files, the environment, and
the command-line values in `options`.

#### Details

The layers are read in npm's order: built-in file, command line, environment, project file,
user file, global file. A later file is found with the layers before it:

- The project directory is `prefix` from the command line, or else the nearest directory, from
  the working directory up, with a `package.json` file or a `node_modules` directory, or else
  the working directory. If a directory above it has a `package.json` whose `workspaces`
  patterns name it, that directory is used, unless `workspaces` is `false` on the command
  line. The project file is skipped in global mode (`global` is `true` or `location` is
  `global`), and when it is the user file.
- The user file is `userconfig`, by default `~/.npmrc`.
- The global file is `globalconfig`, by default `<prefix>/etc/npmrc`, where `prefix` is the key
  or else the global prefix of `options` or the `PREFIX` environment variable.

A file that cannot be read, for any reason, is a layer with no entries, and its error is
kept in [`NpmConfigLayer.error`](#NpmConfigLayer.error). A user or global file that is the same path as a file read
before it is skipped; npm stops with an error in that case. Keys and text values have
`${NAME}` expanded.

#### Errors

- `HostInputError` if the environment or the working directory cannot be read.
- `FileError` with reason `InvalidPath` if the working directory of `HostInput` is not an
  absolute `/` path. Pass `workingDirectory` in `options` to avoid it.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the configuration.

<a id="NpmConfig.impl.parseLayer"></a>

### Associated function `parseLayer`

```silk
pub effect fn parseLayer(
    source: NpmConfigSource,
    file: Option<Path>,
    bytes: &[u8],
  ) -> NpmConfigLayer
    ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator
```

Returns the layer for the ini text `bytes`, with `${NAME}` expanded in keys and text values.

#### When to use

Use it to add text that is not in a file, such as values from your own command line, or to
build a configuration in a test. Add the result with [`NpmConfig.addLayer`](#NpmConfig.impl.addLayer).

#### Details

The text is parsed with `NpmIni.parse`. Keys inside an ini `[section]` are left out. Keys
and text values have `${NAME}` expanded with [`NpmConfig.expand`](#NpmConfig.impl.expand); the items of a `key[]` list
are expanded only for npm's list options `ca`, `cidr`, `diff`, `include`, `noproxy`, `omit`,
`package`, and `workspace`, as in npm. If two keys are the same after expansion, the later one
wins. `file` is recorded in the layer as it is.

#### Errors

- `HostInputError` if an environment variable cannot be read.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the layer.

<a id="NpmConfig.impl.readLayer"></a>

### Associated function `readLayer`

```silk
pub effect fn readLayer(source: NpmConfigSource, path: Path) -> NpmConfigLayer
    ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut FileSystem | &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator
```

Reads the file `path` as the layer `source`.

#### Details

If the file cannot be read, for any reason, the layer has no entries and keeps the error in
[`NpmConfigLayer.error`](#NpmConfigLayer.error), as npm ignores such a file. Otherwise it is the same as
[`NpmConfig.parseLayer`](#NpmConfig.impl.parseLayer) for the contents.

#### Errors

- `HostInputError` if an environment variable cannot be read.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the layer.

<a id="NpmConfig.impl.environmentLayer"></a>

### Associated function `environmentLayer`

```silk
pub effect fn environmentLayer() -> NpmConfigLayer
    ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator
```

Returns the environment layer: one entry for each variable `npm_config_<name>` with a
non-empty value.

#### Details

The prefix `npm_config_` matches in any case. Unless `<name>` starts with `//`, each `_` after
its first character becomes `-` and ASCII letters become lowercase, so `NPM_CONFIG_SAVE_EXACT`
sets `save-exact`. The text `true`, `false`, and `null` become a boolean or a null. Keys and
text values have `${NAME}` expanded. If two variables give the same key, the later one in the
order of the host wins.

#### Errors

- `HostInputError` if the environment cannot be read.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the layer.

<a id="NpmConfig.impl.path"></a>

### Method `path`

```silk
pub effect fn path(self: &NpmConfig, key: string) -> Option<Path>
    ! FileError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the text value of `key` as a path, as npm reads its path options.

#### Details

A value that starts with `~/` is resolved in the home directory. Any other relative value is
resolved in the working directory, and an absolute value is normalized. Returns `None` if no
layer sets `key` as text, or if the value needs a home or working directory that the
configuration does not have.

#### Errors

- `FileError` with reason `InvalidPath` if the value has a NUL byte or goes above the root.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the path.

<a id="NpmConfig.impl.registryFor"></a>

### Method `registryFor`

```silk
pub fn registryFor<'a>(self: &'a NpmConfig, name: string) -> string<'a>
```

Returns the registry URL for the package `name`, as npm chooses it.

#### Details

For a scoped name such as `@acme/widgets`, it is the text of `@acme:registry` if that is set
and not empty. Otherwise it is the text of `registry`, or [`DEFAULT_REGISTRY`](#DEFAULT_REGISTRY). `name` can
also be a spec such as `@acme/widgets@^2`; only the scope before the first `/` is read. The
text borrows from `self`.

<a id="NpmConfig.impl.registry"></a>

### Method `registry`

```silk
pub fn registry<'a>(self: &'a NpmConfig) -> string<'a>
```

Returns the text of `registry`, or [`DEFAULT_REGISTRY`](#DEFAULT_REGISTRY) if it is not set or empty. The text
borrows from `self`.

<a id="NpmConfig.impl.credentialsFor"></a>

### Method `credentialsFor`

```silk
pub effect fn credentialsFor(self: &NpmConfig, url: string, registry: string) -> Option<
    NpmCredentials
  >
    ! OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns the credentials npm would send with a request to `url`, or `None` if there are none.

#### Details

The lookup starts with the key prefix `//<host>/<path>` of `url`, without the scheme, the user,
the query, and the fragment, and with a default port left out. While the prefix is longer than
`//`, it checks `<prefix>:_authToken`, then `<prefix>:_auth`, then `<prefix>:username` with
`<prefix>:_password`, then `<prefix>:certfile` with `<prefix>:keyfile`, and stops at the first
prefix that has one of them set to a non-empty value. Otherwise it removes the last path name
or the last `/` and tries again. So `//npm.test/team/:_authToken` covers
`https://npm.test/team/pkg`.

If no prefix has credentials, and `registry` is a different URL on the same host and port as
`url`, the credentials of `registry` are used, as npm does for tarball URLs. Pass the result of
[`NpmConfig.registryFor`](#NpmConfig.impl.registryFor) for the package as `registry`.

Credentials only for a host-wide key, such as an `_authToken` with no `//host/` prefix, are not
used, as npm 9 and later refuse them.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the credentials.

#### Gotchas

It returns `None` if `url` is not a valid absolute URL.

<a id="NpmConfig.impl.nerfDart"></a>

### Associated function `nerfDart`

```silk
pub effect fn nerfDart(url: string) -> Option<String>
    ! OutOfMemoryError

```

Returns the key prefix npm uses for the credentials of `url`, such as `//registry.npmjs.org/`
for `https://registry.npmjs.org/some/pkg`.

#### Details

It is `//`, the host with a port that is not the default, and the path up to and with its
last `/`. The scheme, the user, the query, and the fragment are left out. Returns `None` if
`url` is not a valid absolute URL.

#### Errors

- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.

<a id="NpmConfig.impl.expand"></a>

### Associated function `expand`

```silk
pub effect fn expand(text: string) -> String
    ! HostInputError | OutOfMemoryError
    ? &mut HostInput | &mut Allocator
```

Returns `text` with each `${NAME}` replaced by the value of the environment variable `NAME`,
as npm expands `.npmrc` keys and values.

#### Details

`NAME` is one or more characters other than `$`, `{`, and `}`. An unset variable leaves
`${NAME}` as it is; a variable set to empty text gives empty text. For `k` backslashes right
before `$`: if `k` is even, `k / 2` backslashes stay and the variable is expanded; if `k` is
odd, `(k + 1) / 2` backslashes are removed and `${NAME}` stays.

#### Errors

- `HostInputError` if an environment variable cannot be read.
- `OutOfMemoryError` if the `Allocator` cannot supply the text.
